utterances.text: But who were they, these seven or eight persons? Who were they? Did you recognise any one of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who were they? I didn't exactly go there to shake hands. How could I have recognised them? How was I supposed to recognise them? It was impossible to recognise them. You don't do that sort of thing in Bosnia, go over there and shake hands. What you have to do is run as fast as you can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What were they wearing? What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An olive-drab suit and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the last part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What were they wearing? You started saying "an olive-drab suit." Were they all wearing an olive-drab suit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some had those and some had plain clothes, like we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Did you hear them say anything? Were they talking amongst themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Barbarat [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What does "barbarat" mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same people. It was a sign.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But does the word "barbarat" have a meaning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's a sign.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: A sign of what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The sign that they were the same people. How come you don't understand this? Brothers, that they were going around beating people. I don't know how I can make myself clear on this. It's a war sign, a code. For those who were in the military, perhaps they should know. I myself served in Macedonia under Tito, and there never was a better ruler than Tito.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know the ethnicity of these seven or eight persons that you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Turks or Muslims or non-aligned or Bosniaks. I'm not sure what I should call them. Turks is what we've called them since World War II. They have different names now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Mr. Miladinovic, you stated that they were setting fire to the houses. How did they do so? Did you saw or notice that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: Again, we're going back to that. What do you mean I didn't see? I'm not talking off the top of my head. I may not have a piece of paper in front of me to show that, but I have it all in my brain. Here it is, the same thing happening again. That's why I told you about different hamlets, in order not to forget any of them. You see what I'm trying to do here. What do you mean I didn't see that? I have the first and last names. Just off the top of my head, I may not have been to school, but I'll make sure to remember everything. I have all the first and last names, everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think you must have received the wrong interpretation. No one is suggesting that you didn't see what you told us that you saw. Mr. Wubben was just asking you to please give a little bit more details. When you said that they were setting fire to the houses, what did you actually see? This was his question. And you were attacking Mr. Wubben as if he was offending you. Just tell us what you saw with your eyes on that day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With my own eyes, I saw them commanding from Brezov Brijeg, left and right. They were commanding on a white horse from Brezov Brijeg. And then things were burned, one house after another, all at once. And when it came to where I was, I started running. Do you want me to go one house at a time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. I want you to go back to what you have just stated a little bit, and please be patient with me, Mr. Miladinovic, because I wasn't there on that day, so I need to know as much detail as you can give us, provided that you keep to the questions that we are putting to you. It may, again, be a question of interpretation, but I need you to explain a little bit better. What I have here on my screen says, when you started giving me your answer, you said: "With my own eyes, I saw them commanding from Brezov Brijeg, left and right." What do you mean by "I saw them commanding"? "Them commanding"? What do you mean by "them commanding"? Who is "them"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Muslims or Turks. Like I said, there was no one else there, no one to be found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then you said: "They were commanding on a white horse from Brezov Brijeg. Who was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Well, the commander, probably. But it wasn't me, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Did you see the commander on this white horse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you mean I didn't? He tied his horse to something on Brezov Brijeg, and he was firing shots and shouting "left and right." Whether it was Golic from Glogova, or another man, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you wouldn't be able to recognise the person who was on the white horse.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How should I recognise that person? 20 -- it's hard for me to recognise anyone at 20 metres' distance, and this was at 500 metres, maybe even one kilometre, as the crow flies. Impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And do you come to the conclusion that he was the commander or that this person, because I don't even know if it's a man or a woman, that this person was the commander because he or she was on a white horse? Is that the only reason why you think he was the commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was an attack. He gave orders, he had to make plans, he had to do some calculations and see exactly what he would do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But did you hear what he was saying? Did you hear the orders that he was giving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't. He was exercising command both left and right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I won't intervene much more than that. Mr. Wubben, he is back to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: My next question is: You did saw the attackers burning down the houses. How did they actually manage to burn the houses? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: What did I see? Well, we saw them taking things out of the houses and looting things. And later, when I returned, they were taking flour away and beans. Whatever they could find in the houses, they were taking things away and taking it up towards Vrestine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you, because you're not answering the question that Mr. Wubben put to you. You're making Mr. Wubben's life very difficult.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure how I should.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: His question was -- he wants you to tell to us, to explain, to describe to us how they burned the houses? What did they do to burn the houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They carried something, something like jugs, round ones. And it only takes a minute to set fire to a house, like I said before. And then they pour it and it catches fire immediately, as if made of wood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Miladinovic, prior to that setting house -- the houses on fire, was there any looting, as you stated? And what did you actually saw regarding looting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He just said it already. I wouldn't waste much more time on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps you can ask him what he saw being taken out, apart from what he has already mentioned, because he even said that he saw them taking out wheat. So I think you've got enough there. Perhaps you could --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did the --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: They were eating things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Witness, I have a question --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: They were taking livestock away, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please, Witness, I have a question for you. Did the attackers set all the houses on fire? And did they loot regarding all those houses, or was it only a part, what you actually saw?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: What I saw is that nothing was left there, not even a chicken or livestock. They were taking everything away, driving everything away. But like I said before, on the 20th of June, once they had taken the livestock away, they killed the pigs and they carried it off, because they needed stuff to eat. Likewise, on the 28th of August, all the livestock wasn't allowed to burn. It would have been a shame. They took everything away.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Witness, when you mean the 28th of August, do you mean actually that particular date? Because you were stating about the attack on the 8th of August --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: The 8th, not the 28th. The 8th, not the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, my next question is: You stated that in the village of Jezestica, there were 120 households, houses to be specific. Did you notice after the attack how many of those houses had been burned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: 60 up in Brdo. Down in Polje, no. But in Brdo, 60 households, all destroyed. Not a single chicken was left. That's what was done on the 8th of August. Nothing was left intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges, was there ever been a compensation for this damage by these attackers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILADINOVIC
utterances.text: No one ever paid any compensation. Not for my two sons. I had six houses, but what do I care about those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, we will need to stop at 20 to and not a quarter to, so you have another five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I have finalised now part of the attack on August, and my subsequent question is to move to the subsequent attack, if so, and that is a specific area, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we can put it off until Monday, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- I suppose. Mr. Miladinovic, we are going to stop here for today, and we will continue on Monday, and I'm sure we'll be able to finish on Monday and then you can return back home. So that's the end of today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness -- the important thing that I need to have a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I could go on like this until daybreak, just to get it over with, until daybreak, I wouldn't even need to stand up except to go to the lavatory, but that's all. I thank this Tribunal. People's throats were cut during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I want to make sure that you understand what I'm going to tell you now. You are going to have between now and Monday all for yourself. You can relax. I'm sure that the staff will assist you also to make your stay here in The Hague as pleasant as possible. I want to make sure, however, that you do not discuss --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- Mr. Miladinovic, let me finish. I want to make sure that you do not discuss matters that you are giving evidence upon with anyone, neither here in The Hague nor over the telephone. It's against the law for someone who still has to continue the evidence, the testimony, to discuss these matters with anyone until he has finished testifying, and you haven't finished testifying. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. I'm not in touch with anyone, nor am I concerned with the other villages, only my own, those villages in the areas of Bratunac and Srebrenica municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You may escort the witness out. We'll see you again on Monday, Mr. Miladinovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. I thank you so much. I thank you so much. The truth will out. I am an old man. I have spasms in my legs.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters can't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] God bless you all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's all for today. Did you have an opportunity to speak to your client during the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I just want to make sure that there will be no repetition of what happened. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, and you have my explanation for the earlier outbreak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We stand adjourned until Monday. I think we're sitting in the morning, aren't we? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 13th day of December, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.41 p.m.,
